retro.outcome:
What did the user correct? Nothing about the implementation approach itself - both tweaks (auth analytics relocation, hierarchy barrels) were scoped via AskUserQuestion up front (auth: confirmed the architectural read against ARCHITECTURE.md's decision log before coding; hierarchy barrels: confirmed scope to features/* only, not app/routing/routes or platform/observability/sinks, which have documented single-import-site/single-reader invariants that a blind 'barrel everything' pass would have broken). The one real correction was procedural: I initially registered step 5's tests with a synthetic, non-verbatim description instead of real grep-able test titles, which loop step na would have accepted incorrectly if not caught - amended to real titles before recording na.

What did G4 reviewers catch that an earlier phase should have? Both reviewers independently caught that this loop's branch carries a commit (5beceba) from a different, still-open loop (phase-3-tree) whose own G4 finding it resolves - not a defect in this loop's own steps, but a diff-scope hygiene gap: a loop branched from another loop's still-open tip inherits that loop's uncommitted-to-main history, and 'the full diff' (main..HEAD) is not the same thing as 'this loop's own changes' when that's true. Neither Frame nor Plan flagged this branch ancestry as something to check before Review. A cheaper catch: at Frame or Plan time, diffing this loop's own step commits against the branch's merge-base with main (or just noting which upstream loop the branch was cut from) would have surfaced this before G4 spent two reviewer passes re-deriving the same provenance question.

Where did this playbook not answer? s-path.md's Phase 7 (Review) doesn't say what to do when a loop's branch was cut from another loop's tip rather than from main directly - it assumes 'the full diff' cleanly scopes to this loop's own work. When that assumption is false, reviewers correctly flag the foreign commit as an out-of-scope behavior change, and the orchestrator has to reconstruct provenance (whose finding was this, was it vetted, by whom) from scratch by reading the other loop's log - work the playbook doesn't guide. Durable lesson proposed: at triage/Frame, when a new loop is created with 'loop init --parent' or cut from a non-main branch tip, record which upstream loop/commit the branch diverged from in loop.json (or at minimum log it), so G4 diffs can be scoped correctly (this loop's own commits only) and, if the full-branch diff is reviewed anyway, provenance for any foreign commit is one lookup instead of a log-mining exercise. Proposed as a diff to loops/conventions.md or state.md for the user to review, not yet applied.
